evidence: utils/rules.ts:133 defines prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule as `(rule?: Rule) => isGrafanaPromAlertingRule(rule) || isGrafanaPromRecordingRule(rule)`, and both helpers are explicit type predicates (rules.ts:103-109). The repo uses TypeScript 5.7.3 (package.json:252), and since 5.5 TS infers the arrow function as the predicate `rule is GrafanaPromAlertingRuleDTO | GrafanaPromRecordingRuleDTO`. So in rules.ts:172, after `&&`, promRule is narrowed to the Grafana DTO, which now declares `provenance?: string` (unified-alerting-dto.ts:135 adds it to GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase). It type-checks. Other code in the PR depends on the same narrowing and would fail to compile without it: RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:57 and AlertRuleMenu.tsx:73 pass the narrowed promRule to a `GrafanaPromRuleDTO | SkipToken` parameter, and RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:139-142 reads promRule.uid after the guard.

isProvisionedPromRule (utils/rules.ts:171-173) checks prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) first and short-circuits, so it returns false for any non-Grafana rule. It only reads provenance after the rule is narrowed to GrafanaPromRuleDTO, which declares it (unified-alerting-dto.ts:135). This matches the existing isProvisionedRule (rules.ts:167-169), which also returns false for non-Grafana ruler rules. Non-Grafana Prometheus rules have no provenance concept, so returning false is correct and not misleading. At most the PromRuleDTO parameter type could be widened to Rule to match the call site in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:124, but that is cosmetic.

GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:47 renders `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} compact />` with no rulerRule. In AlertRuleMenu.tsx:73-96, canSilence ORs in grafanaSilenceAbility from useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (useAbilities.ts:323: [silenceSupported, canSilenceInFolder && isAlertingRule]), so the 'Silence notifications' item renders (AlertRuleMenu.tsx:126-130) and calls handleSilence. But RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:101-103 only mounts SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, and rule is undefined on this path. Clicking the item sets showSilenceDrawer=true and nothing happens. The drawer needs to accept or derive its data from promRule, or the menu item needs to be gated on rulerRule being present.
